analysis.title: From Macro to Micro
key_insights: Client sentiment is summed up as 'a crisis without a crisis'. Clients in London are mostly directionless, bearish in tilt, and gross positioning is light, so a squeeze tighter would be painful for most.
Long equity/short credit and decomp remain the consensus medium-term trades. Credit, especially cash, is viewed as an asymmetric short at current valuations.
Most clients concede a rally is the most likely outcome into year end, but few have positions for it.

The AI-ecosystem scare has moved from private credit (February) and hyperscaler supply (July) to whether companies can afford higher funding costs. The market is moving from macro to micro, where each earnings print and new issue separates issuers.

Index levels remain sticky while dispersion plays out under the surface. The next wave of AI concern is expected to focus on demand and return on capex investment, so future earnings and the pace of ROI need closer attention, though the author does not turn bearish on AI on this basis alone.

The author attributes the latest AI selloff to oil and rates. Higher inflation prints from persistently high oil prices raised expectations of a more restrictive policy path, rates sold off, and corporate funding concerns followed.

The market is trading as if the US-Iran conflict ends soon and views the oil impact as transitory. A deal could lower oil prices immediately and likely trigger a risk-asset rally, while escalation would hurt the economy through higher energy prices.

The in-line FOMC decision (28 Oct) is viewed as a clearing event. With rates stabilizing and oil's inflation impact remaining local, it should ease the funding-cost argument and support risk assets near term.

The team is cautiously optimistic into year end. Positioning is largely unchanged: receivers, tactical IG/HY compression, a tactical fade of long equity vs short credit in hyperscalers, and low-cost hedges.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDX IG receivers to play for upside as seasonality turns supportive
trade_ideas.rationale: Upside vol in credit has remained sticky and has not picked up meaningfully yet.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical IG/HY compression, and re-enter decomp at better levels
trade_ideas.rationale: Compression has worked in recent weeks and there is more room to run.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical fade of long equity vs short credit in hyperscalers: sell AI CDS vs buy NDX puts
trade_ideas.rationale: Long equity/short credit in hyperscalers has worked, and the cost of credit protection has risen significantly in the last month vs equity.

trade_ideas.description: Hedge with payer spreads and an IG ex-hyperscaler basket
trade_ideas.rationale: Limited loss and low cost structures limit theta bleed.

risk_factors: Escalation in the US-Iran conflict would raise energy prices and hurt the economy in the near term.
Persistently high oil prices could keep inflation prints elevated and policy restrictive.
A squeeze tighter against light, bearish-leaning positioning.
Further doubts on AI demand and return on capex.
Higher funding costs for corporates and new issuers.
